subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the unit of electric current?
questions.explain: Electric current is measured in amperes (A), the rate of flow of charge.

questions.q: A current of 3 A flows through a lamp for 10 s. Using Q = I t, what charge passes through it?
questions.explain: Q = I t = 3 A x 10 s = 30 coulombs.

questions.q: How should an ammeter be connected to measure the current through a component?
questions.explain: An ammeter is placed in series so the same current flows through it and the component.

questions.q: Which equation correctly relates potential difference, current and resistance?
questions.explain: Potential difference equals current multiplied by resistance (V = IR).

questions.q: A component has a potential difference of 12 V across it and a current of 3 A through it. What is its resistance?
questions.explain: R = V / I = 12 V / 3 A = 4 ohms.

questions.q: For an ohmic conductor at constant temperature, what does a graph of current against potential difference look like?
options: A straight line through the origin
questions.explain: In an ohmic conductor current is directly proportional to potential difference, giving a straight line through the origin.

questions.q: What happens to the resistance of a thermistor as its temperature increases?
questions.explain: A thermistor's resistance decreases as temperature rises, making it useful in temperature sensors.

questions.q: In a series circuit, how does the current compare at different points?
options: It is the same everywhere in the circuit
It is largest nearest the battery
It is shared between the components
It is different across each component
questions.explain: In a series circuit there is only one path, so the current is the same at every point.

questions.q: Two resistors are connected in parallel. How does the total resistance compare to the resistances of the individual resistors?
options: It is less than the resistance of the smallest resistor
It equals the sum of the two resistances
It is greater than the largest resistor
It equals the average of the two resistances
questions.explain: Adding resistors in parallel provides more paths for current, so total resistance is less than the smallest individual resistor.

questions.q: A 4 ohm resistor and a 6 ohm resistor are connected in series. What is the total resistance?
questions.explain: In series, total resistance is the sum: 4 + 6 = 10 ohms.

questions.q: In a parallel circuit, how is the potential difference across each branch related?
options: It is the same across every branch
It is shared equally between the branches
It is greatest in the branch with most resistance
questions.explain: Each branch of a parallel circuit is connected across the same two points, so the potential difference is the same for each.

questions.q: What are the voltage and frequency of the UK domestic mains electricity supply?
questions.explain: UK mains is an alternating current supply at about 230 V and a frequency of 50 Hz.

questions.q: What is the colour of the insulation on the live wire in a UK three-core cable?
questions.explain: The live wire is brown, the neutral is blue and the earth is green and yellow striped.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the earth wire in an appliance with a metal case?
options: It is a safety wire that stops the metal case becoming live
It carries the normal working current
It completes the circuit during normal use
questions.explain: The earth wire is a safety wire at 0 V that carries current away and prevents the case becoming dangerously live.

questions.q: Which equation gives the power of an electrical device from potential difference and current?
questions.explain: Electrical power equals potential difference multiplied by current (P = VI).

questions.q: A device operates at a potential difference of 230 V and draws a current of 2 A. What is its power?
questions.explain: P = V x I = 230 V x 2 A = 460 W.

questions.q: Why are step-up transformers used in the National Grid before electricity is transmitted?
options: They increase the voltage so the current is lower, reducing energy lost in the cables
They increase the current to deliver more power to homes
They reduce the voltage to make transmission safer
They convert alternating current into direct current
questions.explain: A higher transmission voltage means a lower current, which reduces heating losses in the transmission cables.

questions.q: What happens when two objects carrying the same type of electric charge are brought close together?
options: They exert no force on each other
questions.explain: Like charges repel and unlike charges attract.

questions.q: An insulating rod becomes negatively charged when rubbed with a cloth. What has happened?
questions.explain: Only electrons move; a negatively charged object has gained electrons from the other material.

questions.q: A charged object creates an electric field around it. How does the strength of the field change as you move away from the object?
options: It becomes weaker as distance increases
It becomes stronger as distance increases
It stays constant at all distances
It is strongest exactly at the edge of the field
questions.explain: The electric field is strongest near the charged object and gets weaker with increasing distance.
